AssayWatch report

2026-11-01

Registry status: 2 active, 1 draft. `draft` is a maintainer sign-off, not a data check: 0 of the 1 drafts here already carry a verified DOI, a taxid and a design year with no open review question. What does vary between entries is oligo provenance, flagged in the note column of every row below.

Detected means predicted to amplify. The denominator is evaluable records only: both primers landed in the right orientation and size range. Records with no amplicon, or too many undetermined bases to judge, are excluded and counted separately. Intervals are Wilson 95%, pooled and per lineage alike. A pooled flag needs the upper bound of the recent interval to fall below the threshold. Declining means the share has also fallen from the baseline (that is drift); low coverage means below threshold without a measurable fall.

A lineage can also flag an assay whose pooled share clears the threshold — that is the point of measuring per lineage. Such a row is marked with its pooled status and its note names the lineage, its share and its own earlier share. The lineage rule is an exact binomial test against the threshold, Holm-adjusted within the assay, so it is looser than the pooled rule, and nothing controls error across assays: read an override as a reason to look at that clade rather than as a measurement of the assay.

Duplication check: not run for this flagged assay: their binding-site footprints are unknown (the calls table includes screens from before the footprint columns were written, or counts diverged records as failures), so nothing can be said about whether the flags rest on duplicated records.
